Health Management Information System

HMIS and health information systems — records, registers, reports, digital health and the nurse’s record-keeping duties.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe HMIS and its components
  • List important records and registers
  • Explain the reporting chain
  • Describe digital health systems

In simple words

An information system is the nervous system of health care: it records who is ill, what care was given and what resources are used.

Registers used in community health

Record Purpose
Eligible couple register Family planning eligible couples
Antenatal register Pregnant women registered and visits
Delivery register Conducted deliveries
Immunisation register Children vaccinated, due and missed
Under-five register Births, weight, illness
Mortality register Births and deaths
Family folder Complete family health record

Reporting chain

  • Daily: outpatient register, treatment and drug records
  • Weekly: births, deaths, immunisation, communicable disease reports
  • Monthly: review and analysis, achievements and gaps
  • Quarterly and yearly: performance and programme review

Digital health systems

  • Electronic health records and hospital information system for fast access
  • ABDM — Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission creates a national health ID and links records
  • Telemedicine consultations through video call
  • Reproductive and child health portals for tracking
  • eSanjeevani is a telemedicine platform of the Government of India

🔴 Record keeping is a nursing duty

Incomplete or delayed records cause missed vaccination, missed referral and missed births. Record immediately, accurately and truthfully, and check the register against the actual visit.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. HMIS = records, reports, analysis and feedback.
  2. Registers: antenatal, immunisation, under-five, mortality, family folder.
  3. Reports follow the chain from sub-centre to district.
  4. Information is used for planning, monitoring and evaluation.
  5. ABDM and eSanjeevani are Indian digital health systems.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Weekly reporting captures births, deaths and communicable disease.
  2. Records must be complete, accurate and confidential.
  3. Feedback to staff improves data quality.
  4. Digital records improve access and reduce error.
  5. Privacy safeguards are essential in digital health.

📌 Memory trick

Good record: A-C-C-T — Accurate, Complete, Confidential, Timely.

60-second revision

  • HMIS records, reports and analyses health data.
  • Key registers: antenatal, delivery, immunisation, under-five, mortality.
  • Reports are daily, weekly, monthly and annually.
  • Information guides planning, monitoring and improving.
  • Digital health: electronic records, ABDM, eSanjeevani telemedicine.

Test yourself

Which is a weekly report item?

Answer: B. Births, deaths and communicable disease are reported weekly to the district.

The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission aims at:

Answer: A. ABDM creates a unique health ID and links electronic medical records across providers.

Which register records children vaccinated?

Answer: B. The immunisation register records each child’s vaccines, due dates and missed doses.

Family folders are used to:

Answer: B. Family folders hold the complete family health record, giving continuity of care across visits.

The main quality of a good record is that it is:

Answer: B. Records must be accurate, complete, confidential and timely.
